canonical.behaviour: Release everything on main as 2.9.0-rc.4 and install it. The version changes from 2.9.0-rc.3 to 2.9.0-rc.4 wherever the package states it (the rules stay 1.9.0). CHANGELOG.md gets a plain-English rc.4 entry: /spar now brings the owner in (grilling before the models start, a stop after the openings, owner choices asked as they come up, owner decisions bind while owner opinions can be challenged, and "agreed" needs both models and the owner), with the known gaps listed (the owner's final say on a proposal both models accepted is untested live; no run of Claude against GPT with the new rules). UPGRADE.md gets an rc.3 to rc.4 section. VALIDATION.md is rewritten from a fresh full run. Then one commit and a push to main, `claude plugin update workflow-axa@gazohhh`, and the 20 Codex copies in ~/.agents/skills replaced from the release ZIP after a full backup, checked by `audit_installation.py --check-global`. The released task's checkpoint says it shipped in rc.4.
operations: replace the 20 workflow-axa folders in C:/Users/Cem/.agents/skills, after a backup
exclusions: no change to how any skill or hook works; release records only
no change to the user's global CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or ARTIFACTS.md (global_policy.py and activate_rules.py --apply are not run)
no force push and no rewrite of published history
skills in ~/.agents/skills that are not workflow-axa's stay untouched
conditions: every installed folder equals the release build afterwards (diff, __pycache__ ignored)
the Codex backup is made and checked before any installed folder is replaced
the full suite and validate pass before the commit
checks: audit_installation.py --check-global reports DISK_MATCH with no missing folder
full suite: python -X utf8 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"
